fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents present the strongest real matches: React, accessibility remediation, Storybook, unit testing, a Next.js booking site and an academic Node/Express/PostgreSQL project. They correctly keep backend experience project-based and do not invent two years of experience, NestJS, Playwright, Docker, regulated-data work or WCAG 2.2 compliance. The professional-experience threshold remains unmet, and responsive design, OWASP knowledge, production backend work and end-to-end testing are not established. The letter expresses willingness to learn privacy requirements rather than claiming existing GDPR expertise.

The main factual weaknesses are the omitted part-time qualifier and the letter's unsupported attribution of Git/GitHub use to the internship. The PDFs are readable and ATS-friendly, although the CV's lightly filled second page could be improved; the candidate's underlying experience threshold remains a likely screening obstacle.
